subject: History
description: Chhatrapati Shivaji's life, military innovations, administration (Ashtapradhan), Maratha Empire foundation, key battles.

questions.stem: When was CHHATRAPATI SHIVAJI MAHARAJ formally crowned at Raigad?
questions.explanation: CHHATRAPATI SHIVAJI MAHARAJ was crowned on 6 JUNE 1674 (Jyeshta Shukla Trayodashi 1596 Shaka) at RAIGAD FORT — establishing the MARATHA EMPIRE as an independent Hindu sovereignty. CORONATION CEREMONY: officiated by Pandit GAGA BHATT of Varanasi (a top Sanskrit scholar) who declared Shivaji a 'Kshatriya' (some priests had questioned his caste). EXPENDITURE: ~50 lakh huns (gold coins) — astronomical for the time. SIGNIFICANCE: First Hindu king crowned in India after centuries of Mughal/Sultanate dominance; established 'Hindavi Swarajya' (self-rule for Indians). MARATHA NEW CALENDAR: started the Rajyabhishek Shaka era. SHIVAJI'S BIRTH: 19 February 1630 (some scholars say 1627) at Shivneri Fort, near Junnar. PARENTS: Shahaji Bhosale (Bijapur general) and Jijabai (educator-mother). DEATH: 3 April 1680 at Raigad, age 50. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Shivaji's coronation' is a UPSC, SSC, MPSC top-history fact — 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise dates of foundational events.

questions.stem: What was Shivaji's SIGNATURE MILITARY TACTIC against Mughal armies?
questions.explanation: SHIVAJI's brilliance lay in GANIMI KAVA (guerrilla warfare) — small mobile units hitting larger Mughal armies and disappearing into the rugged Sahyadri hills. KEY ELEMENTS: (1) SUDDEN AMBUSHES on troop columns. (2) Use of ~250+ HILL FORTS as bases — Raigad, Pratapgarh, Sinhagad, Torna, Rajgad, Shivneri. (3) Lightning-fast strikes; never engaged in pitched battle against superior numbers. (4) Local Konkani/Maratha troops who knew the terrain intimately. FAMOUS TACTICAL BRILLIANCES: (a) AFZAL KHAN ENCOUNTER (1659) — Shivaji used WAGHNAKHA (tiger-claws) hidden in his fist to disembowel Khan during a 'peace meeting' at Pratapgarh. (b) SHAISTA KHAN RAID (1663) — Shivaji's commandos snuck into Pune red-fort, severed Khan's fingers, escaped (a personal humiliation for Aurangzeb's uncle). (c) SURAT SACK (1664) — Shivaji's army looted the Mughal-financed Surat port for ~1 crore rupees of treasure. NAVY: Shivaji established the FIRST INDIAN NAVY (~400 vessels) — earned title 'Father of Indian Navy'. PYQ ANGLE: tactical innovations frequently asked.

questions.stem: Shivaji's council of EIGHT MINISTERS was called:
questions.explanation: ASHTAPRADHAN (literally 'eight chiefs') — Shivaji's PRIME COUNCIL of MINISTERS for administering the Maratha state. THE EIGHT POSITIONS: (1) PESHWA — Prime Minister (later became hereditary; Bajirao I etc. famous Peshwas). (2) AMATYA / MAJUMDAR — Finance Minister. (3) MANTRI / WAQENAVIS — Records Officer (chronicler). (4) SACHIV / SHURUNAVIS — Royal Correspondence Secretary. (5) SUMANT / DABIR — Foreign Affairs Minister. (6) SENAPATI / SAR-I-NAUBAT — Commander-in-chief of military. (7) PANDITRAO — Religious Affairs / Charitable Endowments. (8) NYAYADHISH — Chief Justice. STRUCTURAL INNOVATION: Shivaji broke the Mughal/Bijapur tradition of granting hereditary jagirs (land assignments) — instead his ministers were SALARIED, REVOCABLE, and rotated periodically — preventing power consolidation. ROUTINE: Ashtapradhan met daily; major decisions required council deliberation. INFLUENCE ON LATER EMPIRES: post-Shivaji, Peshwa Baji Rao I (1720-40) effectively became the de-facto head; the Maratha Confederacy emerged. PYQ FREQUENCY: Ashtapradhan structure tested in UPSC, MPSC every 2 cycles. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests Maratha-administration knowledge.

questions.stem: Which Mughal Emperor invited Shivaji to AGRA in 1666, leading to a famous escape?

options.option_text: Bahadur Shah, who was Aurangzeb's son.

questions.explanation: AURANGZEB (r. 1658-1707) invited Shivaji to Agra in 1666 to receive him at his 50th-birthday darbar — but humiliated him by seating him among lower-ranked nobles. Furious, Shivaji demonstrated displeasure and was placed under HOUSE ARREST. THE ESCAPE — 17 AUGUST 1666: in one of history's most legendary escapes, Shivaji had himself + son Sambhaji smuggled out of Agra in BIG FRUIT BASKETS (mithai/sweets baskets, prepared 'as offerings to Brahmins'). They reached Mathura, then Vrindavan, then Banaras, finally Raigad in October 1666 — disguised at various points. CONSEQUENCES: Aurangzeb was livid; Shivaji intensified his anti-Mughal campaigns. The PURANDAR TREATY (1665, with Raja Jai Singh of Amber on Aurangzeb's behalf) had earlier ceded 23 forts to Mughals — Shivaji recovered most by 1670. CULTURAL ICON: this escape is dramatized in countless plays, films, comics. The 'fruit-basket escape' is part of every Indian schoolchild's history syllabus. PYQ ANGLE: Shivaji-Aurangzeb interactions are perennial UPSC, SSC, MPSC content. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests dates + key historical events recall.

questions.stem: Who was the first PESHWA (chief minister) of the Maratha Empire under Shivaji?

options.option_text: Baji Rao I of Pune alone.

questions.explanation: MOROPANT TRIMBAK PINGLE was the FIRST PESHWA appointed by Shivaji in 1674 (at Raigad coronation). He served as the head of the Ashtapradhan administrative council. PESHWA EVOLUTION: under Shivaji, the post was a SALARIED OFFICE — not hereditary. After Shivaji's son SAMBHAJI (1680-1689) and grandson SHAHU (after 1707, post-Mughal release), the Peshwa role became progressively more powerful. From BALAJI VISHWANATH BHAT (1713-1720), the Peshwa's office became HEREDITARY in the BHAT FAMILY — known as the BHAT (Brahmin) PESHWAS. FAMOUS HEREDITARY PESHWAS: Balaji Vishwanath (1713-20), Bajirao I (1720-40, the 'unconquered general'), Balaji Bajirao 'Nanasaheb' (1740-61, lost at Panipat 1761), Madhav Rao I (1761-72, restored Maratha glory), Bajirao II (1796-1818, last Peshwa, defeated at Battle of Bhima Koregaon 1818 ending Maratha rule). FACT: by 18th century, Peshwa effectively ran the Maratha Confederacy; the Chhatrapati at Satara was nominal. PYQ ANGLE: Peshwa chronology is a perennial MPSC, UPSC, SSC topic.

questions.stem: Shivaji's two main land-revenue taxes on conquered Mughal/Bijapur territories were:
questions.explanation: CHAUTH = 1/4 (25%) of land revenue — collected from non-Maratha territories in exchange for not raiding them. SARDESHMUKHI = an additional 10% — claimed as the 'hereditary right' of the Maratha Sardeshmukh (chief). TOGETHER: 35% of revenue — Marathas collected this from Mughal and other states starting from Aurangzeb's later years and into the 18th century. STRATEGIC USE: chauth-sardeshmukhi funded the Maratha military expansion across India — northwards to Lahore, eastwards to Bengal, southwards to Tanjore. By the 1750s, Marathas had become the de-facto ruling power in the north (Pindari raids fed by chauth). HISTORICAL CONTRAST: Marathas didn't generally CONQUER and ADMINISTER all these territories — they extracted revenue while allowing local rulers to remain. This 'tribute system' eventually weakened them; lacking a unified bureaucracy they were vulnerable to British divide-and-rule. AURANGZEB'S DECCAN CAMPAIGN (1681-1707) was driven by his frustration at chauth-collection by Marathas — he died in Deccan, exhausted. PYQ ANGLE: chauth-sardeshmukhi is top-5 medieval-history MCQ.

questions.stem: Shivaji's tutor and chief mentor in his early years (military strategy, ethics, administration) was:
questions.explanation: DADOJI KONDDEV was Shivaji's tutor and JAGIR ADMINISTRATOR for the Pune jagir during his minority. Appointed by his father Shahaji Bhosale, Dadoji trained young Shivaji in: (1) Military strategy and weapons (sword, lance, archery, horseback). (2) Reading, writing, Sanskrit, Persian. (3) Statecraft and administration. (4) Mavla guerrilla traditions of the Sahyadri hills. He died ~1647 when Shivaji was ~17 — Shivaji thereafter independently ran Pune affairs. SAMARTH RAMDAS (1608-1681) was Shivaji's SPIRITUAL GURU later in life — author of the 'Dasbodh', a treatise on ethics, statecraft, and devotion. Shivaji deeply respected Ramdas; some legends say he offered his entire kingdom in symbolic 'bhiksha' (alms) to Ramdas, who blessed it back to him. JIJABAI (mother) was an enormous moral influence — she narrated Mahabharata-Ramayana stories, instilling values of justice and bravery. PYQ FREQUENCY: Shivaji's biographical figures (mentors, generals, family) appear in 1-2 MPSC, UPSC questions per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests detailed biographical knowledge of Shivaji's formative years.
